title: Classifying maps from normalized quotient charts and determinant-line identification
statement:
Let $N,r$ be integers with $0<r<N$, and let $\mathcal I$ be the increasing $r$-subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$. Put $B=\mathbf Z[p_J:J\in\mathcal I]$, with every $p_J$ of degree one [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. For an arbitrary ordered $r$-tuple, let $p_{j_1\ldots j_r}$ be the sorting sign times the corresponding increasing coordinate, or zero if indices repeat. For $I,K\in\mathcal I$ define
$$C_{I,K}(a,b)=p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}k_bi_{a+1}\ldots i_r},\qquad F_{I,K}=p_I^{r-1}p_K-\det C_{I,K}.$$
Here determinants use [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant]. Put $H=(F_{I,K}:I,K\in\mathcal I)$, $A=B/H$ with its induced grading [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and $X=\operatorname{Proj}(A)$ [def-pc-proj], with $U_I=D_+(p_I)$. On $U_I$ let $M^{(I)}$ be the $r\times N$ matrix with identity columns indexed by $I$ and off-pivot entries
$$x^{(I)}_{aj}=p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}ji_{a+1}\ldots i_r}/p_I\quad(j\notin I).$$
Let $j:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^{\binom Nr-1}_{\mathbf Z}$ be the morphism induced by $B\twoheadrightarrow A$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Let $q_X:\mathcal O_X^{\oplus N}\twoheadrightarrow Q_X$ be any locally free rank-$r$ quotient [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-amb-finite-locally-free-module] with local frames on $U_I$ in which its matrices are $M^{(I)}$ and its frame changes are $((M^{(I)})_K)^{-1}$.
For every scheme $T$ [def-pc-scheme] and locally free rank-$r$ quotient $q:\mathcal O_T^{\oplus N}\twoheadrightarrow Q$, put $L=\bigwedge^r Q$ and $s_J=q(e_{j_1})\wedge\cdots\wedge q(e_{j_r})$ [def-sc-sheaf-exterior-power]. Then $L$ is an invertible module (locally a free module of rank one) generated by the $s_J$. The corresponding quotient-line morphism $a_q:T\to\mathbf P^{\binom Nr-1}_{\mathbf Z}$ factors scheme-theoretically through a unique $b_q:T\to X$. On the pivot locus $T_I$ for $q$, in any local frame with matrix $M$, the map to $U_I$ has ring formula $b_q^*(p_J/p_I)=\det(M_J)/\det(M_I)$, and its pullback of $x^{(I)}_{aj}$ is the corresponding normalized entry.
There is a quotient-preserving isomorphism $b_q^*q_X\cong q$. Conversely $b_{b^*q_X}=b$ for every morphism $b:T\to X$. Equivalent quotients yield the same $b_q$, and for every $f:T'\to T$ one has $b_{f^*q}=b_q\circ f$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Thus pullback of $q_X$ gives mutually inverse natural bijections between $\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)$ and isomorphism classes of these quotients. Finally $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\bigwedge^r Q_X$ carries $j^*p_J$ to the ordered wedge of the $J$-indexed images of the standard generators [def-pc-projective-space-twist].

proof.text: The pivot-locus assertion of lem-sfb-plucker-chart-quotient-gluing gives an open cover $T=\bigcup_I T_I$ and a frame $v_a=q(e_{i_a})$ on $T_I$. Apply lem-sc-exterior-sheaf-local-free-comparison with $\mathcal M=Q$, $U=T_I$ and $n=r$: the sectionwise exterior power maps bijectively onto $L(V)$ for every $V\subseteq T_I$. By lem-weil-pbc-exterior-power-free-basis, its basis in top degree is the single wedge $v_1\wedge\cdots\wedge v_r=s_I|_V$. Thus $a\mapsto a s_I$ is an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{T_I}\cong L|_{T_I}$; its section maps commute with restriction by the definition of wedge sections. Hence $L$ is invertible and the $s_J$ generate it. This works for arbitrary, possibly empty or nonaffine, pivot opens.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), pivot subfunctors; exterior basis from algebra.tex, Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra).

proof.text: In any frame $w_1,\ldots,w_r$ of $Q$ on an open $V$, write $q(e_j)=\sum_a M_{aj}w_a$. Multilinearity expands $s_J$ into the sum over all $r$-tuples of row indices. Terms with repeated indices are zero; the term with row tuple $\sigma$ is $\operatorname{sgn}(\sigma)\prod_b M_{\sigma(b),j_b}\,(w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_r)$. The Leibniz formula therefore gives $s_J=\det(M_J)(w_1\wedge\cdots\wedge w_r)$. The adjugate identity shows that a square matrix with unit determinant has inverse $\det(M_I)^{-1}\operatorname{adj}(M_I)$; conversely multiplicativity of determinant applied to an inverse shows its determinant is a unit. Consequently the nonvanishing locus of $s_I$ is exactly $T_I$. On $V\cap T_I$ put $N_I=M_I^{-1}M$. Multiplicativity gives $\det((N_I)_J)=\det(M_J)/\det(M_I)=s_J/s_I$. In particular, replacing the $a$-th identity column of $(N_I)_I$ by column $j$ gives determinant $(N_I)_{aj}$, with the ordered-coordinate sorting sign and zero for repeated indices exactly as in the statement.

source.place: Tag 00DM (section-tensor-algebra), alternating wedge expansion; Tag 07DQ (lemma-matrix-left-inverse), adjugate argument. Determinant multiplicativity is the cited matrix leaf.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points to $(L,(s_J))$, enumerating the finite set $\mathcal I$, to obtain $a_q$ and an isomorphism $a_q^*\mathcal O(1)\cong L$ carrying all coordinate sections to $s_J$. The more explicit existence theorem lem-weil-pbc-sections-morphism-to-proj-polynomial-ring, with base ring $\mathbf Z$, gives a morphism with these same properties, so uniqueness in the functor-of-points theorem identifies it with $a_q$. Its clauses (ii) and (iii), and step 2, give $a_q^{-1}(D_+(p_I))=T_I$ and $a_q^*(p_J/p_I)=s_J/s_I=\det((N_I)_J)$.

source.place: Tag 01NE (lemma-projective-space); Tag 01N8 (lemma-converse-construction), chart ring map, specialized to degree-one polynomial generators.

proof.text: By lem-sfb-plucker-determinant-locus-charts the ring of $U_I$ is the polynomial ring in the off-pivot $x^{(I)}_{aj}$. Send these generators to the entries $(N_I)_{aj}$ on $T_I$. The affine-target correspondence gives a unique $c_I:T_I\to U_I$ with this ring map, even when $T_I$ is not affine. The chart identity $\det M^{(I)}_J=p_J/p_I$ gives $c_I^*(p_J/p_I)=\det((N_I)_J)$. On $T_I\cap T_K$ this sends $p_K/p_I$ to the unit $s_K/s_I$, so the basic-open clause of that correspondence puts $c_I|_{T_I\cap T_K}$ in $D(p_K/p_I)$, which is $U_I\cap U_K$ by lem-weil-pbc-proj-basic-open-intersection (with $d=e=1$). Evaluate the identity $M^{(K)}=((M^{(I)})_K)^{-1}M^{(I)}$ from lem-sfb-plucker-chart-quotient-gluing under $c_I$. It becomes $((N_I)_K)^{-1}N_I=N_K$, precisely the frame-change formula for $q$. Therefore $c_I$ and $c_K$ have identical pullbacks of every polynomial generator of $U_K$, so agree as maps into $U_K$ and hence into $X$. The scheme-morphism gluing theorem produces $b_q:T\to X$. Its coordinate formula is the one just computed; for a single replacement coordinate it is the normalized entry by step 2.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), normalized affine charts and their overlaps; schemes.tex Tags 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine), 01HY and 01JA for the affine correspondence and gluing.

proof.text: By lem-sfb-graded-proj-quotient-twist-comparison, applied to the degree-one generated $B$ and the graded surjection $B\twoheadrightarrow A$, one has $j^{-1}(D_+(p_I))=U_I$, and on these charts $j$ is induced by $B_{(p_I)}\to A_{(p_I)}$, $p_J/p_I\mapsto p_J/p_I$. Hence on $T_I$, both $j\circ b_q$ and $a_q$ take values in the projective standard affine open $D_+(p_I)$ and, by step 4 and step 3, pull back every generator $p_J/p_I$ to $s_J/s_I$. The polynomial chart description in lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-twisting-sheaf-charts and the affine-target correspondence imply equality on $T_I$; scheme-morphism gluing gives $j\circ b_q=a_q$. This constructs an actual factorization of scheme morphisms. For uniqueness, let $c:T\to X$ satisfy $j\circ c=a_q$. Since $U_I=j^{-1}(D_+(p_I))$ as just recalled, step 3 implies $c^{-1}(U_I)=T_I$. Each generator $x^{(I)}_{aj}$ is an ordered single-replacement ratio $p_{i_1\ldots i_{a-1}ji_{a+1}\ldots i_r}/p_I$; its pullback under $c$ is fixed by $a_q$ and equals $(N_I)_{aj}$. The chart polynomial-ring isomorphism and affine-target injectivity give $c|_{T_I}=b_q|_{T_I}$. Gluing gives $c=b_q$.

source.place: Tags 01NE (lemma-projective-space), 01NG (lemma-standard-covering-projective-space), and 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), with the cited affine and gluing statements.

proof.text: Use the given frame of $Q_X$ on $U_I$. The pullback clause of lem-sfb-plucker-chart-quotient-gluing, applied to $q_X$ and $b_q$, gives the pulled-back $I$-frame on $T_I$; its matrix is $N_I$ by step 4. Sending its $a$-th basis section to $q(e_{i_a})$ defines an isomorphism $\alpha_I:b_q^*Q_X|_{T_I}\to Q|_{T_I}$ satisfying $\alpha_I\circ b_q^*q_X=q$. On $T_I\cap T_K$, the pulled-back frame change for $Q_X$ and the frame change for $Q$ are both $((N_I)_K)^{-1}$, by lem-sfb-plucker-chart-quotient-gluing. Thus the $\alpha_I$ agree. The morphism-gluing clause of lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules glues them, and also their local inverses; uniqueness in that clause makes the composites identities. The resulting $\alpha:b_q^*Q_X\cong Q$ preserves the quotient. Moreover any quotient-preserving map between the same quotients is unique: the images of the $N$ standard generators determine it, since those generators locally span the targets.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), quotient frames and sheaf gluing; sheaves.tex Tag 04TN (lemma-glue-maps) for gluing the local comparison and its inverse.

proof.text: Let $b:T\to X$ and let $q=b^*q_X$. On $V_I=b^{-1}(U_I)$ the pulled-back $I$-frame makes its matrix $b^*M^{(I)}$, so $V_I$ lies in the $I$-pivot locus for $q$. The construction of step 4 therefore sends $x^{(I)}_{aj}$ to $b^*x^{(I)}_{aj}$ on $V_I$. As $U_I$ has polynomial coordinate ring, affine-target injectivity gives $b_q|_{V_I}=b|_{V_I}$. The $V_I$ cover $T$ by the determinant-locus chart theorem, so scheme-morphism gluing gives $b_{b^*q_X}=b$. Together with step 6 this proves both inverse identities on quotient isomorphism classes. Only containment of $V_I$ in a pivot locus is needed here.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), normalized-chart inverse to the quotient construction.

proof.text: If $\beta:Q\cong Q'$ preserves the quotient, then on $T_I$ it carries $q(e_{i_a})$ to $q'(e_{i_a})$ and every $q(e_j)$ to $q'(e_j)$. Thus the pivot opens and normalized entries coincide, and the affine-chart construction and morphism gluing give $b_q=b_{q'}$. For $f:T'\to T$, lem-sfb-plucker-chart-quotient-gluing says the pivot opens for $f^*q$ are $f^{-1}(T_I)$ and its normalized entries are the pullbacks of those for $q$. On each such open both $b_{f^*q}$ and $b_q\circ f$ consequently have the same polynomial coordinate map into $U_I$; affine-target injectivity and morphism gluing give equality. The pullback identities $\mathrm{id}^*\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $(h\circ g)^*\cong g^*h^*$ in def-pc-module-pullback give the corresponding functor on quotient classes. Steps 6 and 7 now supply mutually inverse natural bijections.

source.place: Tag 089T (lemma-gkn-representable), functoriality of quotient classes and pivot subfunctors; normalized-coordinate verification of naturality.

proof.text: Take $T=X$ and $q=q_X$. Step 7 with $b=\mathrm{id}_X$ gives $b_{q_X}=\mathrm{id}_X$ (using invariance under the canonical identity pullback from step 8). Step 5 then gives $a_{q_X}=j$. Applying the coordinate-preserving isomorphism in lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-functor-of-points to this quotient yields $j^*\mathcal O(1)\cong\bigwedge^r Q_X$ and sends every $j^*p_J$ to the ordered wedge of the $J$-indexed generator images. This proves the final identification with its sections, rather than just an abstract line-bundle isomorphism.
